107 days in 2024-03-10 to 2024-06-28 have a second reading (at 09:00) besides the 08:00 reading; kept the 08:00 reading and dropped the extra one.
One instantaneous reading per day (not a daily mean). In the file's time zone (US/Central): 08:00 on 51615 days, 09:00 on 4 days; in UTC: 14:00 on 30155 days, 13:00 on 21464 days.
USGS 07032000 returned no recent gage height; no extension.

Record low in this file: -11.97 ft on 2023-10-17 (08:00 reading). The National Weather Service lists -12.06 ft that day, which is likely the lowest instantaneous value rather than the morning reading.
USGS: staff gauge 1,000 ft downstream from September 1932 to December 1934, then a recorder below Harahan Bridge from 1934-12-22, about 1.3 miles below the old Beale Street gauge, at the same datum.

The MVS location record for Memphis-Mississippi has no coordinates (0, 0). Lat/lon and the gauge zero (183.91 ft NGVD29) come from the MVK (Vicksburg District) location record for the same gauge. USGS 07032000 lists 184.03 ft NAVD88 for the same zero.
Levels are rounded to 0.01 ft: the API converts from stored meters and returns float noise such as 12.979999999999999.

measurement_history.fact: Mississippi River Commission stage record at the Beale Street gauge begins in November 1871.
USACE Rivergages daily history for the Weather Bureau gauge starts in 1885; its daily value is the 8:00 a.m. Central reading.
Weather Bureau published Beale Street gauge readings from December 1890 to August 1932.
From September 1932 to December 1934, readings came from a staff gauge 1,000 ft downstream of the present site.
A water-stage recorder began at the present site, 50 ft below Harahan Bridge, about 1.3 miles below Beale Street; earlier gauge was at the same datum.
USGS said to add 0.3 ft per 10 ft of stage at the present site to match old Beale Street readings.
USGS listed gauge zero as 183.91 ft (1929 datum), 184.21 ft mean Gulf level (1912), and 190.86 ft Memphis datum (1881).
USGS and USACE now list gauge zero as 184.03 ft NAVD88; date of that update not found.
USGS says the gauge height is furnished by the USACE Memphis District; USGS uses it to publish discharge.
NWS lists the record low as -12.06 ft on Oct. 17, 2023, after -10.81 ft (2022) and -10.70 ft (1988).
Riverbed lowering at Memphis: not found in USGS, NWS, or USACE pages checked (USGS site page, NWS gauge data, Rivergages).

public_notes: Readings began at the Beale Street gauge in 1871 and moved about 1.3 miles downstream in the 1930s, where high-water readings run slightly lower. Gauge zero is a fixed reference point, not the river bottom, so readings below zero are normal in low water; the publishers checked here do not say how much riverbed change has added to recent record lows.
